text: Release operations—from commit to live metrics
A production-minded delivery system with container security, Infrastructure as Code, Helm deployment, and observable runtime behavior.

Open with the product: DeployFlow gives a team one place to plan, promote, and observe service releases.
Explain that every screenshot in this deck was captured from the working local system.
Release decisions need an operational home
DeployFlow turns scattered deployment context into a visible, auditable workflow.
Capture service, version, owner, risk, target environment, and change summary.
Move a release through planned, running, succeeded, or failed states.
Live status metrics surface risk concentration and release outcomes at a glance.

Demo creating a deployment, then update its status.
The domain and interface were redesigned from the starter material to avoid a copy-only submission.
One delivery path, seven verifiable layers
The same application moves from source checks to containers, Kubernetes, and telemetry.
Immutable images are tagged with the commit SHA, scanned, and promoted through Helm values.
Non-root workloads, health probes, resource limits, ingress routing, and autoscaling are encoded—not remembered.
Prometheus scrapes the API; Grafana turns request behavior into a live operational signal.

Walk left to right: interface, API, database, container build, CI, cluster release, monitoring.
All runtime layers are represented by checked-in configuration.
Release CRUD, aggregate statistics, health, readiness, and Prometheus metrics are built in.
Create, validate, list, fetch, update, delete, stats, health, and readiness paths are covered.
Each test suite overrides the database dependency with an in-memory SQLite engine.
Swagger documents every endpoint and schema directly from the running application.

Run pytest -v during the live demo if time allows.
Point out the /health, /ready, and /metrics endpoints that support operations.
Compose proves the full stack. GitHub Actions enforces tests, builds, vulnerability policy, and immutable image tags.

text:
The containers run as non-root users and expose explicit health checks.
The Trivy action is pinned to an immutable action commit and fails on HIGH or CRITICAL findings.
GitHub-hosted run proof requires pushing this local repository to the student's own destination repository.
AWS architecture is explicit before it is expensive
Terraform defines a two-AZ VPC, private worker subnets, NAT egress, and a two-node managed EKS group.
Public and private subnet pairs are generated from the selected AWS region.
Private workers, managed nodes, Kubernetes 1.36, and module/provider constraints are versioned.
Plan/apply are intentionally pending valid AWS credentials; no cloud result is fabricated.

Terraform init and validate succeeded locally.
The current local AWS token returns STS InvalidClientTokenId, so plan/apply/destroy proof must be captured after valid credentials are supplied.
Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/kubernetes-versions.html and https://registry.terraform.io/modules/terraform-aws-modules/eks/aws/latest
The Helm release is running—not hypothetical
A local kind cluster verifies the chart, services, ingress routing, probes, and multi-replica workloads.
Frontend, backend, and PostgreSQL stay internal; ingress is the controlled entry point.
Base, development, and production values separate resource and scaling choices.
Readiness/liveness probes, resource requests and limits, security contexts, and HPA are templated.
